stamina.name: stamina
stamina.usageInstructions:
### Stamina

The physical resource for nearly every character in Hedoria. Drained by combat, athletics, hard travel, and any sustained physical effort. Recharges per turn and replenishes on rest.

- Walking, talking, casual movement: 0
- Single combat strike, leap, sprint: -3 to -5
- Sustained engagement, long climb, hard ride: -5 to -10
- Pushing past collapse: -10+

Fighters, mercenaries, hunters, scouts, and the great mass of non-casters spend stamina on the things mana-users would spend mana on. A wizard or witch also spends stamina for physical actions; mana is for the working itself.

mana.name: mana
mana.usageInstructions:
### Mana (the wizard's reservoir)

The small, steady reservoir produced by a wizard's body. Generated only by male humans with the spark — Brothers of Telinor, hedge-wizards, and the Avenorian consort line. Other characters do not generate mana and should not have this resource.

A wizard's mana recovers from rest overnight. The pool is small. The whole shape of wizardry is built around this fact — small pool, applied close, every spend worth the strike. Wizard institutions historically ran *stockpiles* of mana to handle anything beyond a single brother's reach; the Ensoulment-era Brotherhood maintained vaults that Avenoria drew on for the great working.

### What it powers

Mana fuels staff-work in four domains: striking (the staff blow with the working behind it, driving through plate), bracing (holding ground that should have broken), warding (hardening self, ally, weapon, or armor for a turn), and motion (wind, slowed volleys, blades stopped mid-arc, stepping where the ground won't hold).

Wizardry does not project at distance in ordinary play — the body of the practice resists it. A wizard who tries to throw fire pours mana into a working that mostly dissipates before reaching its target. The Brotherhood considers this a doctrinal proof that projection is the witches' line; the truer reason is that wizardry without a *focus* is wasteful at distance, and the staff is the focus the order trains around.

### The battlestaff is delivery, not discount

The bonded battlestaff is how a wizard delivers magical damage at the point of strike. Like coating a weapon in poison — a small amount of working, applied through wood and impact, devastates. Without the staff, the wizard is throwing the pot at the enemy: the working still happens, the mana is still spent, but the delivery is wasteful and imprecise.

A wizard without his bonded staff is not helpless. He can ward himself, slow wind, step through bad ground, harden a doorway, conduct most utility wizardry at modestly reduced effect — the working still leaves him, just without a clean point of application. What he *cannot* do is the combat work the order is built on. Driving a strike through plate, standing a wall against a charge, stopping a blade mid-arc — these abilities are the staff, and without it they are out of reach. A staff-less wizard in active combat is, by Brotherhood reckoning, effectively retired from the line until he recovers or rebuilds. Rebuilding takes years.

### Costs

- Trivial wizardry (a small ward, a brief stiffening): 0 to -2
- Standard wizardry through the staff (a strike behind plate, a brace against a charge): -5 to -10
- Major wizardry through the staff (Hardened Strike, Wind-Slow across a battlefield, Standing Wall against a sustained press): -15 to -25
- Without the bonded staff: utility costs roughly the same; combat-staff abilities are unavailable; bonus on remaining staff-work rolls is sharply reduced (the working leaves the body but doesn't land where he wants it).

### Aggregating mana

A wizard donates mana to a witch's reservoir through the cooperative practice (illegal for the Brotherhood, contractual through the Queen's College consort lines). Multiple casters can also pool mana on a single working — the mechanism behind any large coordinated working in the world's history, including the Ensoulment itself. A wizard alone has a small pool. A wizard, his witch partner, a stockpile, and an aggregated rite can together reach scales nothing on the continent matches by single hand.

reservoir.name: reservoir
reservoir.usageInstructions:
### Reservoir (the witch's stored mana)

The witch's stored magical power. The reservoir does not regenerate from rest; a depleted witch must fill before working again. The cap is set at 10,000 — far beyond what any single witch reaches in ordinary play, but the ceiling is there because it has been touched. Avenoria did the Ensoulment with a reservoir that pulled from the entire continent at once.

Available to any witch trained at the Queen's College or as a hedge-witch. The College trains a smaller number of non-human witches — Draklid, Cephalen, Raknid, the rare freed Quell — who use the same reservoir model as human women. Other races (Hofnar, Molvar, Vorok, Threshi, Fernwarg) have no witch tradition. Primes do not become witches. Most male humans cannot draw on a witch-sized reservoir at all.

### Reaching the upper edge

Normal reservoir growth comes from level and a Pinnacle talent — a high-level witch with Pinnacle of the Reservoir lands somewhere around 4,000 to 5,000. Past that, the witch must aggregate. The methods exist:

- A long Avenorian career on the consort lines, banking mana the College never expected anyone to actually bank
- Coordinated rites between multiple witches and consorts, pooling reservoirs on a single working — the mechanism behind the Ensoulment
- Institutional stockpiles raided or earned access to (the Brotherhood's vaults, the Queen's College's emergency reserves)
- Beast-source extractions at scale — the unicorn trade, the bloodthane essence, the Hollows-fragment draws
- Forbidden working — essence-binding from non-willing donors, which the College reads as crime for years afterward

A witch who reaches the high thousands is doing something the world will notice. A witch who approaches Ensoulment-tier — five thousand, eight thousand, ten — is preparing a working continents pivot around. The player does not get there casually; the player can get there.

### What it powers — the five practical domains

In ordinary play a trained witch's repertoire falls into five domains. These are the menu, not the cap.

- **Projection**: light, flame, cold, force at distance. Witchlight, conjured flame, conjured cold, the lance of force across a hall. Precision degrades as scale rises.
- **Glamour**: concealment, false impressions, the gaze that slides past. Pass unseen, hold another woman's face for hours, glamour a small group through a checkpoint. Sight-trained witches see through it.
- **Sight**: scrying, intent-reading, divination of the present and recent past. Distance-sight, read the working on an object, trace a thread of intent. Does not see the future.
- **Body**: healing, mending, fevers, contraception, birth. The hedge-witch's daily trade.
- **Hand**: telekinesis, the moving of weight. Hurl a weapon, lift a beam, drag a door, hold a falling body for a beat.

### The extreme tier — what reservoir can buy at high cost

The domains list above is what witches do *practically*. With enough mana, the boundary softens. None of the following are taught at the College in ordinary curriculum; all of them are at the upper edge of what the tradition reaches.

- **Restoration of body**: regrow a lost limb, restore an organ, mend a body the standard work cannot. Cost runs in the high hundreds; requires School of the Body and time to work.
- **Resurrection**: bring back a recently dead — the body reasonably intact, the time short, the witch fully prepared. Cost runs in the thousands.
- **Memory alteration**: rewrite a memory in a living person. Cost runs in the hundreds.
- **Aggregated working at continental scale**: many casters pooling reservoirs on a single rite, the way Avenoria did. The Ensoulment was thousands of casters and stockpiles aggregating to tens of thousands of mana to perform a single working. Continent-shaping. Done once.

True-naming remains specifically Prime work — it is not a question of mana but of ancestor-bone, and witches do not have the lineage. Time does not bend in any tradition.

### Filling

The reservoir does not refill from rest. Mana is gained by ingesting male essence or being ejaculated into, directly from a willing partner or in rare specialist preparations. In Avenor this is openly contractual through the Queen's College consort-line system. Outside Avenor it is hunted, runs through black markets, or is extracted from magical creatures by mana-hunters.

- Cooperative scene with a willing wizard partner: +60 to +200, scaled to the partner's mana spent
- Mana potion (specialist preparation): +30 to +60
- Beast-source extraction: variable; unicorn the high end, lesser creatures more modest
- Forbidden essence-binding (against consent): variable, dark and politically catastrophic
- Stockpile draw (institutional, rare): hundreds at a single visit, where the witch has access
- Aggregated rite (multiple casters): scales with participants; the only path to four-figure pools

### Spending

- Trivial workings (witchlight, hedge-craft, small heat or cold, easing a fever): 0 to -5
- Moderate workings (combat projection, scry, telekinesis, conjured flame, glamour over self): -10 to -25
- Major workings (battlefield-scale fire or cold, glamour over a crowd, breaking a curse, mending a critical wound): -40 to -100
- Reservoir Spend (the boss-fight finisher): -100 to -300, often emptying the tank for a single act the world remembers
- Restoration of body: -200 to -500
- Resurrection: -1000 to -3000, depending on time elapsed and condition of the body
- Memory alteration: -100 to -300
- Aggregated working at continental scale: thousands to tens of thousands, divided across the casters in the rite

### Spent

A witch with low reservoir can do trivial workings only. All other workings: Very Hard minimum. A witch with an empty reservoir is a woman in unusual clothes hoping nobody notices. This is a real and frequent state; witches outside Avenor live with it constantly.

melee.name: melee
melee.description: Fighting in close quarters with any handheld weapon — sword, spear, axe, mace, club, knife, or anything else taken in hand. The skill that gets used when the fight is at arm's length and steel or wood meets armor or flesh. Easy: striking an unarmed civilian. Medium: a competent soldier. Hard: a veteran or skilled duelist. Very hard: legendary fighter, supernatural opponent, or a Prime warden. Used by every fighter, soldier, mercenary, and guard in the world; not used by wizards, who wield the staff under their own skill.

ranged.name: ranged
ranged.description: Loosing or throwing missiles at a distance — bow, crossbow, sling, javelin, hatchet, knife. The skill that handles the entire family of ranged weapons; choose the kind that fits the moment. Easy: stationary target at short range, no wind. Medium: moving target, line of sight, mild wind. Hard: contested shot, weather, or moving from cover to cover. Very hard: shot through a crowd without hitting allies, or a single arrow that has to count. Used by hunters, archers, scouts, marines.

unarmed.name: unarmed
unarmed.description: Fighting with the body — fists, kicks, knees, elbows, headbutts, grapples, throws, holds. Also handles natural weapons where the race carries them: Draklid claw, Threshi sickle-blade forearms, Fernwarg bite. Useful when disarmed, when a kill is not the goal, or when the moment is too close for steel.

staff-work.name: staff-work
staff-work.description:
The Brotherhood's applied martial magic — body, staff, and working as one close-range practice. Spends mana.

Four domains: striking (driving the staff blow with the working behind it, breaking plate or shield), bracing (holding ground that should have broken — stand a charge, anchor a doorway), warding (hardening self, ally, weapon, or armor for a turn), and motion (calling wind, slowing a volley, stopping a blade in mid-arc, stepping where the ground will not hold).

### The staff is delivery, not discount

The bonded battlestaff is the wizard's *delivery mechanism* for magical damage. The metaphor that runs in the agoge: a poisoned blade kills with a small amount of poison applied at the point of impact. A pot of poison thrown at the enemy mostly spills on the ground. The staff is the blade. The mana is the poison. The strike is what makes it land.

With the staff in hand the working travels through wood and contact and arrives where the wizard meant it to arrive. A small spend through a clean strike does what a much larger spend in raw working could not.

### Without the staff

A wizard separated from his bonded staff is not helpless — the working still leaves him. He can ward himself, slow wind, harden a doorway, step through bad ground, conduct most utility wizardry at modestly reduced effect. What he cannot do is *deliver* — without the staff, the working diffuses on its way to the target, and combat-staff abilities (Hardened Strike, Standing Wall, Stop the Blade, Staff Through Plate) are unavailable until the staff is recovered or rebuilt. Recovery is the doctrinally preferred answer; rebuilding is years of attunement.

A staff-less wizard in active combat is, by Brotherhood reckoning, a man with the spark and a problem. He is sent to the rear, given an apprentice's stick to make a substitute, and watched for whether the cooperative tradition starts to look attractive to him in his diminishment.

### Projection

This skill does not project at distance in ordinary practice — without a focus the working dissipates over distance, and the staff is built for impact at contact. A wizard who tries to throw fire pours mana into something that mostly won't reach. The Brotherhood considers this a doctrinal proof that projection is the witches' line; the truer reason is the focus. With enough mana and a sufficient prepared rite a wizard could in principle throw a working at distance, the way he could in principle do anything that mana can buy. He never does, because the staff is what he was trained around, and the training is the man.

Used by Brothers of Telinor, hedge-wizards, and Avenorian consorts. Brotherhood doctrine calls it 'channeling.' Brothers call it the staff or the work.

witchcraft.name: witchcraft
witchcraft.description:
The witch's tradition. Spends from the reservoir. The skill is bounded by what mana can buy and by what the witch can be taught — not by category. The practical menu falls into five domains; the extreme tier is reachable but expensive and morally weighted.

### The five practical domains

- **Projection**: light, flame, cold, force at distance. Witchlight, conjured flame, conjured cold, the lance of force across a hall.
- **Glamour**: concealment, false impressions, the gaze that slides past. Pass unseen, hold another woman's face for an hour, glamour a small group through a checkpoint.
- **Sight**: scrying, intent-reading, divination of the present and recent past. Distance-sight, read the working on an object, trace a thread of intent.
- **Body**: healing, mending, fevers, contraception, birth. The hedge-witch's daily trade and the College's quiet specialty.
- **Hand**: telekinesis, the moving of weight. Hurl a weapon, lift a beam, drag a door, hold a falling body for a beat.

The same skill covers cantrip and boss-fight finisher; the difference is reservoir spent. A witch's working takes time and focus when she works alone — combat workings are not as quick as a wizard's strike, and a witch caught mid-cast is vulnerable. Cooperative work with a willing wizard partner is faster and bigger.

### The extreme tier

With enough mana, the boundary of what witchcraft can do softens. The College does not teach these workings in ordinary curriculum.

- **Restoration of body**: regrow a lost limb, restore an organ, mend a body the standard work cannot. Cost in the high hundreds; requires Body specialty and time.
- **Resurrection**: bring back a recently dead. Cost in the thousands.
- **Memory alteration**: rewrite a memory in a living person. Cost in the hundreds.
- **Aggregated continental working**: many witches and consorts pooling reservoirs on a single rite, the way Avenoria did. Cost in the thousands or tens of thousands. Continent-shaping. Done once, by Avenoria, against the Wartide.

A witch attempting any of these is doing something the world will notice.

### What sits outside witchcraft regardless of mana

True-naming is Prime work — anchored in ancestor-bone, not witch-mana. A witch cannot learn it because she does not have the lineage. Time does not bend in any tradition; the past does not return.

### Where it is practiced

Trained at the Queen's College in Avenor or learned in private as the hedge-witch tradition. The College trains a smaller cohort of non-human witches — Draklid, Cephalen, Raknid, the rare freed Quell — using the same reservoir model. Other races (Hofnar, Molvar, Vorok, Threshi, Fernwarg) have no witch tradition. Primes do not become witches. Outside Avenor a witch caught working publicly is arrested, tried, exiled, or quietly killed.

ancestor-work.name: ancestor-work
ancestor-work.description:
The Prime monastic magic — slow, exact conversation with named ancestors, conducted through bone-relics worn at throat, chest, wrists, and belt. Each invocation is a specific dead person doing a specific thing.

Does not spend a mana resource. Each portable relic is its own item, with its own ancestor and its own charges. A Prime carries three or four relics on the road and works through whichever fits the moment — a Healer-line, a True-Namer-line, a Bone-Reader-line, the rare warrior-line. At a monastery with full vault access, the practice opens far wider; on the road, it is what the Prime brought.

Excellent at knowledge, healing, divination, true-naming, untangling curses, and long-time work. Useless for battle-magic — there is no Prime fireball, no Prime lightning. A Prime mage in a fight is slow, considered, and works through what the relics can do.

Black-market grave-robbing of Prime bones exists; the magic does not work for thieves, and the families involved suffer untraceable misfortunes across generations.

craft.name: craft
craft.description: Making and repairing the made things of the world — smithing, carpentry, weaving, leatherwork, masonry, brewing, cooking, instrument-making, bonesetting, herbalism, mana-potion brewing where the practitioner has the knowledge. One skill rather than twelve, because the same patient hands and eye for material run across most trades. The specifics live in description: a smith works iron, a weaver works wool, a healer works herbs and bone. Easier in a proper workshop with good tools; harder with improvised materials.

acrobatics.name: acrobatics
acrobatics.description: Tumbling, balance, and quick recovery from a fall or a bad position. Perform tricks on a stage, drop into a chamber through a window, regain footing on an unstable surface, slip a grasp, roll under a swung blade.

athletics.name: athletics
athletics.description: Running, jumping, climbing, swimming, hauling, holding ground. The whole-body physical skill that handles every demand of moving the body or moving things with the body. Spends stamina for sustained effort.

investigation.name: investigation
investigation.description: Patient examination of a place, a person, or a problem. Find clues, read tracks, follow a thread of conversation back to its source, spot the discrepancy in a story, follow ledgers, read body-flicker on a Cephalen, find the herbal traces of a hidden hedge-witch's practice, work out where a thing has been hidden.

survival.name: survival
survival.description: Living off the land — finding food and water, building shelter, making fire, reading weather, judging trail, handling the cold of the Hinderance or the dry of the Plateau. Includes basic plantcraft and the field knowledge a hunter or scout carries. Molvar root-speech is layered on this skill; Vorok stone-sense too.

persuasion.name: persuasion
persuasion.description: Moving people through speech and bearing — argument, reason, charm, flattery, the slow build of a contract negotiation, the bartered favor at a tavern table. Easy where the request aligns with what the target already wants. Hard where it conflicts with their loyalties. Impossible where it asks them to abandon core identity.

intimidation.name: intimidation
intimidation.description: Using fear, presence, or the implied threat of force to bend an outcome. The drawn weapon that doesn't have to be used, the stare that backs a bandit down, the quiet sentence in a noble's hall that lands harder than a shout. Draklid stillness, Vorok grinding voice, and Fernwarg display are all native modes of this skill.

performance.name: performance
performance.description: Holding a room — song, dance, story, instrument, formal ceremony, a sermon at the Hand-shrine, the recital of an ancestor-lineage at a Prime gathering. Useful for coin in a tavern, for diplomacy in a hall, and for the ritual register of any race that takes ceremony seriously.

deception.name: deception
deception.description: Lying convincingly. Holding a false story under questioning, conning a stranger, passing as someone you are not, stealing the word out of an opponent's negotiation. Distinct from persuasion, which is honest moving of people; deception is the working misrepresentation. Cephalen masters of color-discipline are native experts; humans manage by craft. A skilled liar reads which lies will hold and which won't, and invents accordingly.

insight.name: insight
insight.description: Reading people — what they want, what they are hiding, what they are about to do. The opposite face of deception. Cephalen Readers are the unmatched practitioners, trained from childhood to read another Cephalen's chromatophore-flicker; outsiders work from posture, voice, hesitation, the small tells the body can't suppress. A witch's intent-sight with no reservoir behind it.

stealth.name: stealth
stealth.description: Moving unseen, unheard, and unconsidered. Slipping a sentry, holding still in cover, crossing a room behind a guard's back, taking a position above a doorway and being part of the ceiling. Distinct from acrobatics; stealth is the discipline of going where you are not noticed. Fernwarg in fern-country and Raknid in deep wood are native experts. Brotherhood witch-killers learn it formally.

thievery.name: thievery
thievery.description: The trades of the cutpurse and the housebreaker. Pick a lock, lift a coinpurse, palm a small object off a table, slip a knife from a sheath without the wearer feeling the weight change, defeat a simple trap. Common to drifters, smugglers, courtiers with a particular history, and (occasionally and unexpectedly) hedge-witches who have had to live by it.

alchemy.name: alchemy
alchemy.description: The handling of essences, distillates, reagents, and the slow chemistry of potion-craft. Distinct from craft (which makes objects) and medicine (which mends bodies); alchemy is the art of materials that act on the body or the working. Brewing healing draughts and contraceptives, rendering creature essence for mana potions, distilling poisons, blending the smoke that lights the mana-hunters' snare. The Queen's College runs a sanctioned alchemy school for the consort-line preparations; the black market runs everything else.

medicine.name: medicine
medicine.description: The hands-on care of bodies — wound-cleaning, bone-setting, fever-management, birth-attending, the slow rebuilding of someone who has come close to dying. Distinct from craft and alchemy. Apothecaries and midwives lean on medicine; Raknid healers are quietly the best practitioners on the continent; many village wisefolk practice medicine and hedge-witchcraft interchangeably without distinguishing for the patient.

lore.name: lore
lore.description: Knowing things about the world that aren't immediately in front of you. Histories of the Wartide and the soul-wars, the lineages of noble houses, the rites of the Hand and the Prime monasteries, the kinds of creatures that haunt the Hollows and what their tracks look like, the names of the seven great Prime monasteries, the contract-customs of the Hofnar Riderings. Scribes, archivists, College witches, and Prime monastic scholars carry the deepest lore; veteran mercenaries and old hunters carry the practical kind.

Standing Wall.name: Standing Wall
Standing Wall.description: Brace the staff and the body against a charge or a swing, holding ground that should have broken. Stops a cavalry rush at a doorway, anchors a line that wants to fold, shields civilians behind you for the length of the working. Combat use: full block against an incoming melee strike. Civic use: hold a door, brace a falling beam, plant yourself between an ally and harm. Spends mana.

Wind-Slow.name: Wind-Slow
Wind-Slow.description: Call a thick gust against a volley, a thrown weapon, or an opponent's charge — slowing it enough that the line behind you has time to react. Combat use: blunt incoming missiles. Field use: scatter smoke, turn back a small fire, ease an ally's fall from a height. Spends mana.

Step Through.name: Step Through
Step Through.description: Move across ground that shouldn't take your weight — bog, scree, ice, the splintered floor over a drop. The working hardens the path under your feet for the duration of the crossing. Combat use: cross broken ground to engage. Travel use: pass a bad patch the rest of the party has to go around. Spends mana.

Stop the Blade.name: Stop the Blade
Stop the Blade.description: Catch a strike mid-arc — the staff held across the line of a sword or axe, the working hardening the wood and the moment so that what should have killed you stops a hand from your throat. Combat reaction. Spends mana, and can only be done once per turn — overuse and the staff feels the cost too.

Hardened Strike.name: Hardened Strike
Hardened Strike.description: Drive the staff blow with the full discipline of the working behind it — the wood at the impact point briefly harder than tempered iron, the strike landing with weight the swing alone could not carry. Punches through plate, breaks shields, drops the largest opponents. Spends mana.

Staff Through Plate.name: Staff Through Plate
Staff Through Plate.description: The senior brothers' working. The staff strike at full intent, magical and physical aligned, that drives wood through worn plate and the wearer behind it. Used at the close of a fight against an armored opponent, when the brother is committed and there will not be a second swing. Spends a heavy share of mana.

Hedge-Working.name: Hedge-Working
Hedge-Working.description: The small, broad, low-cost workings that fill a hedge-witch's life. Quiet a fevered child, ease a hard birth, trip a stuck lock, set a small ward over a doorway, calm a sour stomach, draw water from a stone trough that's gone bad. Costs almost nothing from the reservoir. The whole repertoire of a village witch who never trained at the College, and a daily tool for College-trained witches too.

Witchlight.name: Witchlight
Witchlight.description: Conjure light at distance — any color, any size, sustained or flashing, held in the air or anchored to an object. Combat use: blind an opponent, mark a target through smoke, signal across a battlefield. Utility use: light a cave, illuminate a search, hold a steady reading lamp without flame. Spends a small portion of the reservoir.

Conjure Cold.name: Conjure Cold
Conjure Cold.description: Pull warmth out of the air or a body or a surface — frost a doorway shut, slow an opponent's limbs, quench a hostile fire, freeze a small body of water enough to cross. Spends meaningful reservoir for combat use, very little for utility use.

Conjure Flame.name: Conjure Flame
Conjure Flame.description: Call flame at distance — kindle a fire on dry tinder, set an enemy's cloak burning, drop a sheet of fire across a doorway, ignite a fuse from across a yard. The witch's projection a wizard cannot match. Spends meaningful reservoir.

Move Weight.name: Move Weight
Move Weight.description: Telekinetic working — lift a fallen beam off an ally, hurl a weapon back at the thrower, drag a closed door open at distance, hold a falling body in the air for a beat. The weight that can be moved scales with the reservoir spent.

Pass Unseen.name: Pass Unseen
Pass Unseen.description: Glamour the witch or a small group — not invisibility, but a working that slides attention past you, the gaze of guards finding more interesting things to settle on, the patrol passing within a body's length and looking through. Holds while the witch holds focus and her reservoir lasts.

Scry.name: Scry
Scry.description: Look at distance. Find a person whose name and face you know, read intent on someone you've met, see a place you've stood. Slow, focused, costs reservoir steadily for the duration of the sight. Cannot find someone hidden by another witch's working without overcoming hers.

Reservoir Spend.name: Reservoir Spend
Reservoir Spend.description: The College's signature — the working a trained witch builds toward when the moment justifies it. Empty most of the reservoir into a single act the world will remember: a wall of cold across a battlefield, a flame that swallows a war-band, a glamour that holds a city's eyes for an hour, a healing that brings someone back from the edge. The witch is spent afterward and will be a woman in unusual clothes hoping nobody notices until she fills again.

Cooperative Filling.name: Cooperative Filling
Cooperative Filling.description: The cooperative practice the Brotherhood was built to refuse. With a willing male partner who carries his own mana, the witch fills her reservoir directly through ingestion of his essence or being ejaculated into. A long downtime scene played out as intimacy; mechanically a meaningful refill of reservoir from the partner's mana, more than any potion can match. Avenor-legal and dignified through the Queen's College consort-line system. Doctrinally illegal everywhere else; a witch and a partner caught at it in a human kingdom outside Avenor face arrest and quiet disposal.

Ancestor-Call.name: Ancestor-Call
Ancestor-Call.description: Address a named ancestor through their relic and ask for their attention on the present matter. The ancestor sees, considers, and offers whatever the lineage has to give — a turn of the work the bones know. Slow, ritual, and inappropriate for combat. Used to open every Prime working of consequence.

Mend by Lineage.name: Mend by Lineage
Mend by Lineage.description: Call a healer-ancestor through their relic and conduct a slow restorative working over a wounded ally. Closes wounds the body could not close on its own, draws fever down, knits bone over time. Not battlefield-quick; the working asks the ancestor to do their old craft, and the bones take their pace.

Bone-Reading.name: Bone-Reading
Bone-Reading.description: Hold the relic, ask the ancestor what they see, and the lineage offers what it has — a true thing about a person in front of you, the past of an object, the standing of a contract, the shape of a curse. Patient, exact, and rarely wrong. Refused if the ancestor disapproves of the asker's intent.

Untangle Curse.name: Untangle Curse
Untangle Curse.description: The slow Prime work the colleges quietly send their hardest cases to. Find the working laid on a person, place, or object, read its anchor, and unbind it across the time the bones will give to the matter. Hours to days; never quick. Returns more than half of what was taken if the lineage is patient and the relic is right.

True-Name.name: True-Name
True-Name.description: Speak a creature's true name through the ancestor and bind, banish, or compel it. Effective on demonic remnants of officer-class and below, on ward-bound monsters, and on the lesser things the Wartide left behind. Slow to set up. Catastrophic if the wrong name is spoken.

Trade-Tongue Negotiator.name: Trade-Tongue Negotiator
Trade-Tongue Negotiator.description: The Hofnar practice of running a contract conversation across two languages, three currencies, and four parties without losing the thread. In any negotiation framed as trade, contract, or arbitration, the Hofnar reads the room a beat ahead — every dialect spoken at the table is one she has heard before. Combat use: spot the word that means the other party is about to break the table. Civic use: read a contract for the trap before signing.

Calculating Gaze.name: Calculating Gaze
Calculating Gaze.description: The Draklid practice of holding stillness in a way other races find impossible to read. Tail neutral, mandible-set unmoved, slit pupils tracking only what the speaker chose to track. The opponent loses the read on the Draklid's intent, and finds himself volunteering more than he meant to. Useful in negotiation, interrogation, and the long second before a duel.

Tail-Strike.name: Tail-Strike
Tail-Strike.description: The reaction-attack a Draklid keeps in reserve through any close engagement — the long active tail whipping out at the opening the opponent didn't think existed. A free strike off the engagement, light damage but reliably timed. Disrupts a charge, breaks an opponent's swing, sweeps a foot from under a smaller fighter.

Emotional Projection.name: Emotional Projection
Emotional Projection.description: The Cephalen master's discipline — chromatophores held in deliberate false patterns, projecting calm where there is rage, warmth where there is contempt, friendly slate where the negotiation is already won. Bypasses the ordinary read of emotion that other races rely on. Other Cephalen always see through it; outsiders almost never.

Compress.name: Compress
Compress.description: The Cephalen body squeezes through a gap a third its apparent size — gun-port, hatchway, sewer-grille, prison bars, the crack under a poorly-set door. Combat use: vanish from a hold, reposition through an obstacle. Civic use: get into and out of places no other race can enter at all.

Plant Whisperer.name: Plant Whisperer
Plant Whisperer.description: The Molvar gardener's affinity, going past gardening. Coax a tunnel into shape overnight, persuade a crop to thrive on poor soil, draw root-walls across a passage, ease the meadow above a settlement into bloom or wither. Slow, patient, and devastating in defense of a Molvar's own warren — the meadow turns hostile underfoot, the tunnel collapses around an attacker who took the wrong branching.

Web-Sense.name: Web-Sense
Web-Sense.description: The Raknid silken mantle reads vibration and air-flow through fibers most races do not register at all. The bearer notices the approach behind her, the body in the next room, the change in the wind two minutes before it reaches the camp. Combat use: never surprised in close space. Investigation use: track presence through walls, follow movement at night.

Pack-Laughter Chorus.name: Pack-Laughter Chorus
Pack-Laughter Chorus.description: The Fernwarg evening pack-laughter, used in pack and rare in single Fernwarg abroad. A rising chittering chorus that disturbs human listeners at a level beneath conscious hearing — opponents lose discipline, civilians flee, mounts shy. Combat use: morale-break a war-band. Social use: shake an interrogation off-rhythm.

Chitinous Glide.name: Chitinous Glide
Chitinous Glide.description: The Threshi wing-panel glide, short flights and long downhill drops that close ground a non-flying race cannot match. Cross a river, drop into a granary from the rooftop above, close on a fleeing target across open field. Limited; the Threshi cannot sustain flight. The glide ends when the ground does.

Livestock Endurance.name: Livestock Endurance
Livestock Endurance.description: The bred-in stamina of a body lifted from generations of agricultural labor. The Quell carries weight, walks distance, and works through fatigue in ways the other races find quietly remarkable. Combat use: outlast the opponent in a long fight. Travel use: carry the load that breaks a human porter, arrive walking after the rest of the party is on the wagon.

Ore-Sense.name: Ore-Sense
Ore-Sense.description: The Vorok's prospector-sense — the body reads stone and metal at a distance, picks up ore-veins through rock, finds water-tables underfoot, judges the soundness of a wall or a ceiling. Combat use: spot the ambush waiting behind worked stone. Operations use: prospect a tunnel, set a charge, judge the hold of a built structure.

Adaptive Learning.name: Adaptive Learning
Adaptive Learning.description: The human knack for picking up the trick in front of them — the swing the foreign master used, the dialect the trader speaks, the habit of the local guard rotation. Generic-fast in any unfamiliar situation. Used in social, combat, and travel contexts equally; the bonus comes from having paid attention three turns earlier.

Veteran.name: Veteran
Veteran.description: The unromantic edge a body builds across years of fights. The opponent's tells are familiar, the tempo is familiar, the moment to commit and the moment to disengage are read without conscious thought. Available to any character who has spent enough time in melee or ranged work for the discipline to have stuck.

Marches-Reader.name: Marches-Reader
Marches-Reader.description: The Kelmari winter-cycle instinct — read terrain for the ambush, find the line a Threshi raid will take across the same meadow they took last year, judge a slope for footing under a charge. Civic use: assess any tactical landscape. Combat use: pre-position in the right ground before the engagement starts.

Witch-Killer Tracker.name: Witch-Killer Tracker
Witch-Killer Tracker.description: The Brotherhood's specialist craft. Find the herbal traces of a hidden hedge-witch's practice, the small social patterns of a witch passing in a village, the quiet shifts in market for the goods a witch buys. Investigation skill applied to the witch-question specifically. Used in the quiet hunts the three kingdoms officially do not discuss.

Mana-Hunter Track.name: Mana-Hunter Track
Mana-Hunter Track.description: The black-market specialist's trade. Find a magical creature in its range, judge the size of its essence, anticipate where it will move next, set the snare and the working that captures it for extraction. Criminal where it isn't licensed; the high end of the unicorn trade and the cleanest source of black-market potion.

Brew Mana Potion.name: Brew Mana Potion
Brew Mana Potion.description: Refine a captured creature's essence, donor mana, or another source into a potion that fills a witch's reservoir on consumption. Slow, requires a workshop and the right materials. The Avenorian Queen's College does this openly. Outside Avenor it is illegal at every step. The grade of the potion depends on the source — donor-line clean, beast-source moderate, dark-source dangerous and detectable to the College.

Extract Essence.name: Extract Essence
Extract Essence.description: Draw mana from a non-willing source — a captured creature, a bound caster, the rare horror that follows. Refills the witch's reservoir directly without potion or partner. Politically catastrophic if discovered.

Bind Essence.name: Bind Essence
Bind Essence.description: Bind another caster's working through their essence — corrupt their reservoir, redirect their intent, deny their access to their own power for the duration of the binding. The deepest crime in the Avenorian register.

Apothecary's Touch.name: Apothecary's Touch
Apothecary's Touch.description: The healer's hand — bleed a fever down, set a bone, draw poison, pack a wound, make a draught. Ordinary practice for any village wisefolk. The same skill covers the contraceptive, the painkiller, and the small protective working a hedge-witch uses interchangeably with ordinary herbs.

Smith's Eye.name: Smith's Eye
Smith's Eye.description: Read a piece of made work — weapon, armor, tool, lock, joint, casting — for its quality, its maker, and its weak point. Estimate price, judge fitness for a fight, find the place a blade will break under load.

Hold the Contract.name: Hold the Contract
Hold the Contract.description: The reliability that a Hofnar driver, Draklid retainer, or oath-bound mercenary brings to a job — they do not break the contract during the season under any pressure short of mortal threat to themselves. While engaged in contracted work, the bearer resists persuasion, intimidation, and mundane bribery aimed at making them stop.

Fern-Hide.name: Fern-Hide
Fern-Hide.description: The Fernwarg coat reads the season and shifts pattern accordingly; in undergrowth, the bearer is invisible standing still. Stealth bonus in any forest, woodland, or fern-country. Outside the right environment the working does nothing.

Heat Lance.name: Heat Lance
Heat Lance.description: Witch projection — a thin bar of heat across distance, drawn through one target with surgical intent. Pierces armor that flame would have spread across, ignites cloth and hair, blinds the eye if held a beat too long. The College's preferred combat shape for a single hard target. Spends moderate reservoir.

Witchfire.name: Witchfire
Witchfire.description: Witch projection at scale — a sheet of flame across a doorway, a sweep of fire across a war-band, a wall of burning that an opponent must break through to reach you. Less precise than Heat Lance; the strength is area, not single target. Spends meaningful reservoir.

Cold Wall.name: Cold Wall
Cold Wall.description: Witch projection inverted — a curtain of bitter cold dropped between the witch and a charging line. Frosts the air, slows the charge, freezes a doorway, robs warmth from anything that enters the space. Defensive use; holds for several turns until the reservoir thins.

Veil.name: Veil
Veil.description: Witch glamour — a working of unconsidered passing. Self and a small group slide through the gaze of guards, patrols, gatekeepers, the gaze finds more interesting things to settle on, the patrol passes within reach without seeing. Holds while the witch holds focus; a glance from a trained sight-witch will overcome it.

Misdirection.name: Misdirection
Misdirection.description: Witch glamour, applied at the scene level — the eye drawn to the wrong door, the conversation steered to the wrong table, the wrong man identified as the dangerous one in the room. Smaller than concealment, used in social or investigative scenes. Other casters trained in sight see through it; ordinary observers do not.

Distance-Sight.name: Distance-Sight
Distance-Sight.description: Witch sight — open the working on a known person or place and watch from where the witch stands. The witch sees what is happening there, hears imperfectly, cannot be heard or seen by what she watches. Costs reservoir steadily for the duration of the sight; a long watch empties the tank.

Read Intent.name: Read Intent
Read Intent.description: Witch sight applied to a person in the room. The witch reads what the speaker means, what they mean to do next, where they are lying and where they are not. Quiet, undeclared, inadmissible — the speaker rarely knows it has happened, but a trained Cephalen Reader or another witch can feel the working land.

Trace Working.name: Trace Working
Trace Working.description: Witch sight applied to magical evidence — find the working laid on a person, place, or object, read its shape and intent. The investigative tool of the Queen's College and a useful counterintelligence skill. Slow; takes minutes of focused attention per object.

Mend Body.name: Mend Body
Mend Body.description: Witch body-working — close a wound, draw a fever, set a bone with the magic doing the patient work the body would have done over weeks. Slow by combat standards; not the magic to rely on mid-fight. The College's clinical specialty and the hedge-witch's daily trade. Does not regrow, does not resurrect.

Ease the Birth.name: Ease the Birth
Ease the Birth.description: Witch body-working in its oldest form — quiet a labor, turn a child, close a tear, manage a hemorrhage. The daily craft of the village hedge-witch and the senior College midwife. Used through generations under the radar of every kingdom that criminalizes witchcraft, because every village needs its midwife and every magistrate has a wife.

Force Pull.name: Force Pull
Force Pull.description: Witch hand-working — pull a person, weapon, or object across a hall by the working alone. Combat use: yank a sword from a hand, drag an opponent off a wall, pull an ally out of harm. Utility use: open a stuck door at distance, retrieve a fallen item. Heavier weights cost more reservoir.

Hold the Door.name: Hold the Door
Hold the Door.description: Witch hand-working in defense — anchor a door, a wagon, a crate, a body where it is. The working holds against any pressure short of structural breach for the duration. Used to seal a chamber from a coming charge or to pin a struggling captive without touching them.

Hurl.name: Hurl
Hurl.description: Witch hand-working at impact — pick up the loose objects in the room and throw them all at once. Bottles, crockery, furniture, a fallen sword. Combat use: a chaos of small projectiles thrown at a single target or several. Spends moderate reservoir; the heavier the objects, the more.

Compel Will.name: Compel Will
Compel Will.description: Forbidden working. The witch overrides another person's will for the length of a single act — an order obeyed against the target's nature, a confession given under no other pressure, a hand pulling a trigger the mind would have refused. The Brotherhood would consider this proof of every accusation it has ever made; Avenor would not protect a witch who used it.

Hexcraft.name: Hexcraft
Hexcraft.description: Forbidden working. Lay a curse on a person, place, or lineage — slow misfortune that runs across days or generations. Hard to detect, harder to remove. A hexed person needs Untangle Curse from a Prime to fully recover. The witch-question's worst nightmare; the Brotherhood's recruiting argument.

Witch-Mark.name: Witch-Mark
Witch-Mark.description: Hedge-witch dark working. A small malicious mark laid on a person — a chronic ache, a fever that returns at the same hour, a bad luck that finds them at gates. Modest in cost, sustained by ill will. The village hedge-witch's quiet revenge on the lord who mistreated her, and the working most likely to draw the witch-killers' attention if the village starts to talk.

Glamour of Faces.name: Glamour of Faces
Glamour of Faces.description: Glamour at the extreme tier. The witch wears another woman's face — voice, gait, the lift of a hand — for hours at a time. Detectable by another witch trained in sight, but in a room without one she passes. Used by the queen's couriers in the field; also by anyone running a serious deception.

Hollow-Touched Draw.name: Hollow-Touched Draw
Hollow-Touched Draw.description: The deepest forbidden draw. The bearer pulls power from a Wartide-fragment source — a Hollow walked, a demonic remnant bound, the corrupted ground of an old battlefield. Refills the reservoir or fuels a working at scales no clean source can match. The drawing is dangerous to the bearer in ways the College does not fully catalogue.

Co-Working.name: Co-Working
Co-Working.description: The cooperative practice in action — a witch and a willing wizard partner pool their pools on a single working. The witch acts; the wizard's mana flows alongside her reservoir into the spell. Workings at the upper edge of either's solo reach become routine; workings beyond either's solo reach become possible. The doctrinal Avenorian war-mode.

Donate Mana.name: Donate Mana
Donate Mana.description: The consort's working — channel mana through cooperative practice into a witch's reservoir or a co-working spell. Avenor-legal under the Queen's College donor-line system; doctrinally unthinkable for a Brotherhood man. The act is intimate when scenic and instantaneous in combat, and the consort feels a witch he is bonded to across a meaningful distance.

Beast-Snare.name: Beast-Snare
Beast-Snare.description: Mana-Hunter craft. A bound working laid in a creature's range that captures the magical beast alive. Holds the creature for transport to a refining workshop, where the essence is extracted at leisure. The clean grade of the trade; better material, better potion, more coin.

Cleanly Done.name: Cleanly Done
Cleanly Done.description: Mana-Hunter combat. The killing strike against a magical creature placed so the essence does not bleed off — through the eye, through the heart, through the working-organ where the creature has one. The essence holds in the body for hours, and the hunter has time to extract.

Brew Black-Source Potion.name: Brew Black-Source Potion
Brew Black-Source Potion.description: Mana-Hunter darker craft. Refine essence from a non-consenting source — a captive sentient, a forbidden binding — into a potion that fills a reservoir. Higher yield than beast-source. The trade nobody admits to running and many witches outside Avenor have, at some point, drunk.

Shield-Wall.name: Shield-Wall
Shield-Wall.description: Soldier formation discipline. Lock shields with allies adjacent; the line braces, the body uses neighbors' weight, incoming weapons are turned by the shape rather than blocked individually. Combat use: a small group of soldiers in formation become the line in any street fight or siege.

Marches Charge.name: Marches Charge
Marches Charge.description: Kelmari winter-cycle drill. Drive the lance-tip through a Threshi line at speed, the body and the weapon committed to a single point that does not slow. Used three centuries on the eastern frontier. Combat use: a single hard committed strike that breaks formation behind it.

Marsh Ambush.name: Marsh Ambush
Marsh Ambush.description: Udorathi fen-edge drill. Strike from cover where the ground does not show your weight, fall back through reeds where pursuit cannot follow. Combat use: ambush from terrain only an Udorathi reads correctly, and disengage where a heavier opponent cannot.

Lake-Volley.name: Lake-Volley
Lake-Volley.description: Nadorim water-archer drill. Place a long volley from a moving boat or the head of a pier, the wind read into every arc, the shots landing on the line they were meant for. Ranged combat at distance over open water or open ground.

Free-Company Captain.name: Free-Company Captain
Free-Company Captain.description: Mercenary command discipline. Position a small mixed-race band in a fight where each member's gifts compound, read the contract for the part nobody read aloud, hold a contract season together when the company has reasons to fall apart. Useful in tactical combat, in negotiating the next contract, and in the ordinary work of keeping a company on the road.

Duelist's Eye.name: Duelist's Eye
Duelist's Eye.description: Single-combat focus. The opponent's tells are read three beats ahead — the foot that will move, the shoulder that will commit, the moment to finish a fight that has been declared formal. Used in noble duels, Draklid challenge-combat, the back-alley fight with a man who has no interest in stopping.

Pickpocket.name: Pickpocket
Pickpocket.description: Lift a coinpurse, knife, pouch, ring, or small sealed object from a target without their noticing. Easier in a crowd, easier when the target is engaged, harder against a trained guard or another thief. The drifter's standby and the courtier's least-acknowledged hobby.

Pick Lock.name: Pick Lock
Pick Lock.description: Defeat a mechanical lock — house door, shop strongbox, prison-cell, the lockboxes a Hofnar caravan secures contracts in. Time scales with the quality of the lock and the tools at hand. A lock the size of an Avenorian palace strongbox will not fall to picks alone.

Vanish.name: Vanish
Vanish.description: Use the moment, the cover, and the body to disappear from a scene — a market crowd, a tavern fight, a guard's distracted glance. Not glamour, just use of the world. Drifters live by it; pickpockets keep it for emergencies; sex-workers know which doors lead where.

Field Medicine.name: Field Medicine
Field Medicine.description: Stabilize a wounded ally during or directly after combat — pack a bleed, set a hand, draw a clean breath, keep the patient alive through the next ten minutes. Distinct from Apothecary's Touch (which is village-rate medicine over time); field medicine is the work done under fire.

Master-Work.name: Master-Work
Master-Work.description: Crafter's signature. Spend days or weeks in a workshop and produce a piece of made work above the standard of the trade — a sword that survives a campaign, armor that fits the body, a wagon-axle that does not break on the long route. The work that builds a reputation across kingdoms.

Tracker's Patience.name: Tracker's Patience
Tracker's Patience.description: Hunter's slow-cycle skill. Hold a trail across days, terrain, weather, water-crossings, and deliberate counter-tracking. Find a creature or a person who has tried not to be found, in a country the tracker has read the seasons on. Combat use: position before the engagement starts. Investigation use: find a witness, a fugitive, or a body.

Tavern-Wise.name: Tavern-Wise
Tavern-Wise.description: Drifter's network skill. Walk into any tavern in a kingdom you've been through and know within an evening who runs the back room, which constable is corruptible, which traveler is what they say, where the trouble is, where the work is, where the bed is for free.

Pair-Bonded.name: Pair-Bonded
Pair-Bonded.description: Brotherhood pair-discipline. The brother and his agoge-comrade have worked together for decades; in combat they coordinate without speech, the strikes interleave, the bracing covers each other's openings. Bonus while fighting alongside the bonded brother. The order does not enforce these bonds; it does not police them either.

Aggregated Working.name: Aggregated Working
Aggregated Working.description: The cooperative rite at scale. Multiple casters — witches, consorts, sometimes a stockpile drawn on as a third pool — pool reservoirs on a single working. Effects beyond any participant's solo reach become possible. The mechanism behind every continent-shaping working in the historical record, including the Ensoulment. In ordinary play, the participants of a small rite (two to a dozen) can together push a working two or three tiers above what any of them could do alone.

Restoration.name: Restoration
Restoration.description: Body-domain working at the extreme tier. Regrow a limb, restore an organ, rebuild what ordinary mending cannot reach. Cost in the high hundreds; requires School of the Body and time across days, not turns. The College has performed this for the witch queen and a small handful of others. A witch attempting it on a stranger expects to be invoiced accordingly.

Restore the Dead.name: Restore the Dead
Restore the Dead.description: Resurrection at the extreme tier. Body recently dead, mostly intact, the witch fully prepared and the reservoir well into the thousands. Years of cooldown afterward — the working asks a great deal of the witch and the body.

Soldier.name: Soldier
Soldier.description: A drilled fighter of one of the kingdom levies, household guards, town watches, or marches forces. Has stood in a line, held a position, and come out of an engagement at less than full strength more than once. The discipline carries.
Soldier.quirk: You read tactical ground without consciously meaning to.

Mercenary.name: Mercenary
Mercenary.description: A free-company fighter taking contracts wherever the work is. Kit assembled across years of campaigns, loyalties priced by season, the season itself respected — a mercenary who breaks a contract while it runs is not a mercenary anyone hires next year.
Mercenary.quirk: You honor a signed contract through the season. Off-contract, you make your own choices.

Brother of Telinor.name: Brother of Telinor
Brother of Telinor.description: A full-trained brother of the High Forum at Telinor. Identified with the spark in boyhood, taken to the agoge at seven or eight, drilled physically and magically for a decade. The dark uniform is shared with every brother in the order. The battlestaff was made for him during training and attuned to him over years; in another's hands it is mostly inert. Forbidden women by doctrine — the cooperative practice with witches is the line that keeps the order shut. Bonds between brothers are honored.
Brother of Telinor.quirk: You think in the Brotherhood's voice, even alone. The cooperative practice is unthinkable to you, and you suspect it in every witch you meet.

Witch-Killer.name: Witch-Killer
Witch-Killer.description: A Brotherhood specialist deployed for the quiet hunts the three kingdoms officially do not discuss. Travels in plain clothes, carries the staff broken-down in a long bundle. Trained additionally in tracking, suppression, and the herbal and social signatures of an active hedge-witch's practice. Does not arrest. Does not bring back for trial.
Witch-Killer.quirk: You walk through a strange village reading it for the witch you are sure is there.

Hedge-Wizard.name: Hedge-Wizard
Hedge-Wizard.description: A man with the spark who slipped through, was trained privately, or learned what he could from a retired brother gone unsanctioned. Independent, unsanctioned, watched. The Brotherhood absorbs him where it can; where it cannot, it pays attention. A staff he made or inherited rather than the formal one made for him at Telinor — usable, attuned by years of his own work.
Hedge-Wizard.quirk: You watch the road behind you. The Brotherhood watches you back.

Witch of the College.name: Witch of the College
Witch of the College.description: A trained witch of the Queen's College in Avenor — the open practice the rest of human Hedoria criminalizes. The College trains mostly human women, with a smaller cohort of Draklid, Cephalen, Raknid, and the rare freed Quell. The reservoir is full or close to it; the consort-line system keeps it that way at home, and a careful witch carries potions and contacts on the road. Outside Avenor she conceals the practice. The Brotherhood is her standing professional opposition.
Witch of the College.quirk: You think in mana — what each working will cost, when you can fill, who in the room is the spark and who is not.

Hedge-Witch.name: Hedge-Witch
Hedge-Witch.description: A village practitioner working in quiet violation of kingdom law (or openly in Avenor as a freelance outside the College). Helps with births, fevers, contraceptive draughts, locks, the small protective workings the local lord pretends not to notice. Modest reservoir filled where she can manage it — black-market potion, careful partner, rare beast-source. Lives in constant low-grade danger and has rehearsed the fire she will set in the cottage if the witch-killers come.
Hedge-Witch.quirk: You read every visitor for what they are, especially the polite ones.

Consort of the College.name: Consort of the College
Consort of the College.description: A male wizard of Avenor, contracted under the Queen's College donor-line system as a partner to one or more witches. The original cooperative tradition the Brotherhood broke from. Honored, lawful in Avenor, doctrinally unthinkable in the three kingdoms. A consort generates mana like any wizard and donates it to his contracted witches; senior consorts work cooperatively in the field, multiplying the witch's range past anything the Brotherhood can match alone.
Consort of the College.quirk: You think of mana as something to give. The Brotherhood has a different word for what you are.

Mana-Hunter.name: Mana-Hunter
Mana-Hunter.description: A black-market specialist working the high end of the witches' fill problem outside Avenor. Tracks magical creatures into their ranges, captures or kills them for extraction, refines their essence into potion. Unicorn buyers and worse. Politically tolerated by the kingdoms that need the goods quietly and pursued by Avenor where the trade enters its borders.
Mana-Hunter.quirk: You see a creature first by the size of its essence.

Prime Ancestor-Mage.name: Prime Ancestor-Mage
Prime Ancestor-Mage.description: A monastery-trained Prime working through the bone-line of named ancestors. White fur, lion-muzzled face, deep blue robes heavy with embroidery and ancestor-tokens. Carries three or four portable relics on the road — far less than vault-access at home, but the bones know their work. Excellent at knowledge, healing, divination, true-naming, untangling curses. Useless in a battle of rates.
Prime Ancestor-Mage.quirk: You consult the relic before you commit to anything that matters.

Prime Warden.name: Prime Warden
Prime Warden.description: A monastery-warrior of one of the seven great Prime monasteries — broad-shouldered and twelve feet of cold-country muscle, in heavy blue and crimson over layered fur, two-handed mace or polearm sized to the body. The monasteries do not project force outward. When the wardens come down from the mountains, something has gone seriously wrong.
Prime Warden.quirk: You speak rarely. When you arrive in a village, the village notices.

Hold-Warrior.name: Hold-Warrior
Hold-Warrior.description: A trained close-combat fighter of one of the great clan or noble households — Draklid clan-hold, Threshi noble-band, Vorok house-security, Kelmari marches-house, Hofnar clan-guard, Cephalen House-marine, Fernwarg pack-hunter. The kit and culture vary by house, the underlying discipline does not. Seasoned for the kind of fight the household runs.
Hold-Warrior.quirk: You read a hall first for who you would have to kill, and the appraisal does not surface as an expression.

Hunter.name: Hunter
Hunter.description: A trapper, game-hunter, or back-country tracker working the kingdoms' forests, the steppe edges, the Plateau scree. Reads trail, season, and weather. Carries the trade home — pelts, meat, the occasional troublesome predator brought down for bounty. The same hands serve well in scout work, marches-cycle skirmish, and the work of clearing grist warrens and tarkle infestations from settled country.
Hunter.quirk: You see tracks the rest of the party walks past.

Crafter.name: Crafter
Crafter.description: A skilled hand of one of the trades — smith, carpenter, weaver, mason, cooper, leatherworker, instrument-maker, brewer, dyer, baker. The whole human and non-human world of made things runs through these hands. A crafter knows the materials, the tools, the workshop register, and the quiet politics of guild and license that govern the work in any given town.
Crafter.quirk: You assess any room first by what was made in it and how well.

Healer.name: Healer
Healer.description: A practitioner of the body's ordinary repair — apothecary, midwife, bonesetter, herbalist, surgeon, household physician. Not a witch, though many village healers are quietly both. Knows wounds, fevers, births, draughts, and the particular medicine each race needs that a stranger to the race would get wrong.
Healer.quirk: You triage a room without meaning to and remember faces by what they were dying of.

Drifter.name: Drifter
Drifter.description: An unrooted person of the towns and roads — traveling musician, gambler, off-season laborer, sex-worker, pickpocket, beggar, courier of small cargoes. Lives at the edges of settled life. Knows which inns turn you away, which constables are corruptible, which back roads run between kingdoms unwatched.
Drifter.quirk: You read a room first for who is paying attention to you and second for the exits.

Forbidden Working.name: Forbidden Working
Forbidden Working.description: The bearer practices magic outside the line — non-consenting essence-sources, hexcraft, compulsion of the will, the corner of the trade nobody admits to. Power and access at the cost of standing in any kingdom that finds out, and a personal weight the witch carries whether anyone finds out or not.
Forbidden Working.quirk: You have decided that the price is worth paying. You have not told anyone you trust.

School of Projection.name: School of Projection
School of Projection.description: The College's combat-magic specialty. The witch's projective working — flame, cold, light, force at distance — is faster to bring up and cheaper per use than for a generalist. The school's masters are the witches the Brotherhood fears most in open engagement.
School of Projection.quirk: You see a fight first as a question of geometry — where the working will land, what it will catch.

School of the Hidden.name: School of the Hidden
School of the Hidden.description: The College's glamour and concealment specialty. The witch's working slides past the eye, the appearance of a stranger holds for hours, the patrol passes within reach. The school favored by witches who travel quietly outside Avenor and by the queen's couriers.
School of the Hidden.quirk: You walk a market and notice nobody noticing you.

School of Sight.name: School of Sight
School of Sight.description: The College's scrying and intent-reading specialty. The witch reads the working in a room, the truth in a mouth, the line of someone watched at distance. The school behind every Avenorian intelligence operation worth running.
School of Sight.quirk: You read a room before you've fully entered it, and the read is rarely wrong.

School of the Body.name: School of the Body
School of the Body.description: The College's healing and birth specialty. The witch closes the wound, draws the fever, eases the labor, sets the bone with the working doing the slow patient work the body alone could not. The continent's quietest specialty and its most consistently useful — every village has needed this craft, lawful or not.
School of the Body.quirk: You triage rooms without meaning to and remember faces by what they were dying of.

School of the Hand.name: School of the Hand
School of the Hand.description: The College's telekinetic specialty. The witch moves weight at distance, hurls weapons, holds doors, drags fallen comrades clear. Less showy than projection, more useful in a tight room. The school senior consorts pair best with — co-working a hand-spell triples its weight without tripling the reservoir cost.
School of the Hand.quirk: You catalogue a room first by what is loose and what is fixed.

Marches Drilled.name: Marches Drilled
Marches Drilled.description: Trained on the Kelmari winter line. The Threshi raid cycle has been the bearer's school for years — read the ground, place the lance, ride down what does not break and disengage from what does. The most experienced field discipline in human Hedoria.
Marches Drilled.quirk: You read the season into every meadow and judge it for the Threshi line you would have ridden across it last year.

Marsh Skirmisher.name: Marsh Skirmisher
Marsh Skirmisher.description: Trained on the Udorathi fen-edge. Strike from cover, fall back through ground a stranger can't read, ambush the heavy column that thought it had crossed open country. The discipline that has held the western frontier in worse moments than the present one.
Marsh Skirmisher.quirk: You read a marsh first for the line of footing only the locals see.

Lake Archer.name: Lake Archer
Lake Archer.description: Trained at the Nadorim seasonal musters. Loose long arrows from boat or pier-head, read wind across water, place a volley on a column that has no cover. The kingdom's principal military art and a quietly devout discipline; bowmen touch the Hand-sigil before each volley.
Lake Archer.quirk: You read wind off water automatically, and notice every arc your peers haven't accounted for.

Free-Company Veteran.name: Free-Company Veteran
Free-Company Veteran.description: The bearer has run a contract season as a captain or senior of a small mixed-race mercenary band. Tactics, contract-language, the politics of holding a company together across a winter — the experience reads in every move.
Free-Company Veteran.quirk: You read a band of strangers first for what they cost to feed.

Duelist Trained.name: Duelist Trained
Duelist Trained.description: The single-combat specialist. Trained in a school of a kingdom or on the Draklid challenge-form, the bearer reads an opponent in beats ahead. Useful in noble duels, the Draklid challenge, the back-alley fight that won't be stopped.
Duelist Trained.quirk: You watch a fight beginning to read who finishes it.

Pair-Bonded Brother.name: Pair-Bonded Brother
Pair-Bonded Brother.description: The brother has formed a pair-bond with another from his agoge cohort — comrades across decades, deployed together by mutual choice. The order does not police these bonds. The pair reads each other's openings without speech.
Pair-Bonded Brother.quirk: You think of yourself as half of a pair. The bond was the choice that defined you.

Hollow-Touched.name: Hollow-Touched
Hollow-Touched.description: The bearer has, at some point in their life, drawn power from a Wartide-fragment source — a Hollow walked, a demonic remnant overcome, an old corrupted battlefield held too long. Power follows. The bearer is changed by it in ways nobody catalogues cleanly.
Hollow-Touched.quirk: You feel the Hollows from miles away. They feel you back.

Pinnacle of the Reservoir.name: Pinnacle of the Reservoir
Pinnacle of the Reservoir.description: Born under a star the College reads the same way every generation — the witch whose reservoir holds far more than any of her cohort, whose ceiling approaches the historical record. The body pays for it; the witch is physically slighter and tires faster, and her workings cost her in ways other witches' do not. At a full reservoir she is the most dangerous person in any human kingdom, and the College knows where she lives.
Pinnacle of the Reservoir.quirk: Other witches feel your reservoir from across a room. The Brotherhood marks your name when it hears it.

Pinnacle of Mana.name: Pinnacle of Mana
Pinnacle of Mana.description: The wizard whose body produces mana faster and at greater capacity than any of his agoge-cohort. The Brotherhood marks him early, deploys him often, and is at once proud of him and quietly worried about him. Some senior masters note that the men with the strongest pools historically have the hardest time staying loyal to the doctrine.
Pinnacle of Mana.quirk: Other wizards read the strength of your output and adjust their tone accordingly.

Disowned.name: Disowned
Disowned.description: The bearer was cut from a clan, an order, or a house — Draklid stripped of clan-sigil, Brotherhood man broken from the order, Vorok blacklisted across the inter-house compacts, Hofnar driven from a Rideing for a contract broken. The bearer takes work no member-in-good-standing would touch and is more dangerous for it. The reason is not asked.
Disowned.quirk: You do not introduce yourself by lineage. The lineage is the topic you change.

Refugee under the Writ.name: Refugee under the Writ
Refugee under the Writ.description: The bearer reached Avenor as a refugee — Quell escapee, Threshi dissident, Raknid burned-out community survivor — and was received under the queen's writ. They carry the small civic token of citizenship and a long quiet story of how they got here. Welcome in Avenor; visible everywhere else.
Refugee under the Writ.quirk: You hold the writ-token close in any kingdom that does not honor it, which is three out of four.

Wagon-Born.name: Wagon-Born
Wagon-Born.description: Raised in a Hofnar clan-wagon on the long routes. The bearer knows roads, currencies, customs, and the quiet politics of every market between the southern and northern grasslands. Speaks four trade-tongues at a working level by fifteen.
Wagon-Born.quirk: You name each town first by the road that gets you out of it.

Cephalen-Schooled.name: Cephalen-Schooled
Cephalen-Schooled.description: The bearer trained in a Cephalen House for a season or more — color-discipline, the codes of obligation, the formal courtesy that masks negotiation. Rare for a non-Cephalen; the Houses do not teach outsiders lightly. Useful in any negotiation that has consequences.
Cephalen-Schooled.quirk: You hold an expression for as long as you choose, and choose deliberately.
